claims.text: This taxonomy is echoed across multiple papers, with Chen et al. (2025) applying it specifically to code generation, and Zhang et al. (2025) examining its interaction with Chain-of-Thought prompting.

Wang et al. (2025) propose Adaptive Test-Time Scaling (ATTS), which dynamically allocates computation based on problem difficulty and model confidence, achieving comparable performance to fixed-budget methods while reducing computation by 40-60%.
Li et al. (2024) address edge deployment with GreenTTS, using early-exit mechanisms and hardware-aware scheduling to achieve 70-85% of full TTS performance with only 30-40% energy consumption.

Wang et al. (2024) explore an orthogonal approach through multi-agent collaboration, distributing computation across specialized agents to achieve comparable performance with 3-5x less total computation.

Xia et al. (2025) address factual reasoning, where TTS is challenging due to open-ended knowledge; their Retrieval-Augmented TTS (RATTS) improves accuracy by 10-18% by grounding candidates in retrieved evidence.

Ge et al. (2026) examine TTS through the lens of on-policy distillation, revealing that distillation improvements do not uniformly extend across all sampling budgets—a critical finding for post-training optimization.
Zhang et al. (2025) conduct a comprehensive empirical study examining how TTS affects CoT across three dimensions: number of samples, chain length, and recursive decomposition depth.

First, TTS consistently improves performance across domains, with typical gains of 8-18% reported across mathematical reasoning (Chen et al., 2025), code generation (Chen et al., 2025), multimodal reasoning (Liu et al., 2025), and factual reasoning (Xia et al., 2025).
Second, all surveyed papers agree that naive compute scaling is suboptimal—adaptive allocation based on problem characteristics is essential for efficiency (Wang et al., 2025; Li et al., 2024).

Third, there is consensus that TTS effectiveness depends on task structure: tasks with clear verification mechanisms (math, code execution) benefit more than open-ended tasks (factual reasoning) (Xia et al., 2025).
Ge et al. (2026) demonstrate that on-policy distillation improvements can reverse at large sampling budgets—improving small-budget performance while reducing large-budget pass@K.

Additionally, while Wang et al. (2024) advocate multi-agent collaboration as more efficient than single-model scaling, other papers assume single-model architectures, suggesting unresolved questions about the optimal architectural paradigm for TTS.

First, adaptive computation allocation remains underdeveloped—while ATTS (Wang et al., 2025) and GreenTTS (Li et al., 2024) demonstrate feasibility, optimal difficulty prediction and confidence estimation across diverse tasks remain open challenges.

Third, integration with retrieval-augmented generation is identified as an open direction by Liu et al. (2025) and partially addressed by Xia et al. (2025), but systematic understanding of TTS-RAG interaction is incomplete.

Finally, the reversal phenomenon identified by Ge et al. (2026) suggests fundamental questions about the relationship between training-time optimization and test-time scaling that require deeper investigation.
